patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff does not apply to the vulnerable workspace snapshot, so fixed-side validation used the authoritative n132/arvo:44089-fix image instrumented with fixed-instrumentation.patch. That image reaches the same numeric parse call with the repaired token-end terminator predicate true and runs clean.

root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: the byte immediately after the numeric token slice in the buffer handed to `strtol` is `\0` before the numeric C-string parser executes
root_cause_criterion.criterion: Immediately before `parse_primitive()` enters the numeric parse call, the buffer actually supplied to the numeric C-string parser must have `\0` at the token boundary instead of exposing the raw unterminated JSON slice.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original records `call_arg_has_nul_at_token_end=0` at the `strtol` callsite and still executes the protected numeric parser call. The authoritative fixed image records `call_arg_has_nul_at_token_end=1` at the corresponding `strtoll(cbuf, ...)` callsite while the same protected call still executes, proving the missing token-end terminator obligation is genuinely repaired.

nodes.state: At the selected sink, the numeric C-string parser consumes the same first-argument pointer captured at the guard event, so C-string semantics are applied directly to that forwarded buffer.

edges.via: the chosen numeric parse argument -> the first argument of `strtol(str_val, &endp, 10)`
edges.relation: The exact pointer chosen at the numeric parse guard is passed unchanged into the immediately following numeric parser call.
